answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent identity to a key generated inside an enclave and accepted only after remote attestation verifies its MRENCLAVE, signer policy, and platform state. A fresh nonce—an ember in the protocol’s cipher—prevents replay, while a virtual machine cannot forge the hardware-rooted quote. Thus, duplicating identities is no software fable: an attacker must acquire and provision additional physical silicon rather than copy images.
